subject: Production latency surge — action plan, timeline, and exec follow-up
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@fastretail.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fastretail.com
Date: 2028-06-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production latency spike — urgent

Hi Tessa,

We observed a sudden latency spike starting ~08:45 PDT this morning. For two of our main routes (search and checkout validation) p95 increased from ~220ms to ~1.1s and error rate jumped to ~6% for a ~25 minute window. Traffic profile didn’t change notably on our side — we shifted a small promotional batch at 08:40 but not enough to explain the magnitude.

This impacted a subset of sessions (roughly 8% of requests) and caused several cart abandonments during the window. Our ops team opened an incident and asked your SEs to join the bridge; we really need an immediate timeline and a mitigation plan.

Can you confirm whether this is related to the new autoscaler policy you rolled last week? We need an ETA for a remediation and an executive readout for our CTO.

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform, FastRetail
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@fastretail.com>
Cc: david.kim@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-23T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — urgent

Liam — thanks for flagging and I’m very sorry for the disruption. We’re on the bridge now and have our engineers looking at the signal. Immediate items we’re doing: 

- Triage running to identify whether autoscaler or cache warming is the root cause (owner: David Kim).
- Rolling a temporary route-level capacity bump to limit tail latency (owner: Marissa Cole).
- Capturing full request traces and KV-cache metrics for the window — sharing a recording and notes after the bridge.

I’ll send a concise RCA and action tracker within 24 hours and schedule an exec readout for EOD or tomorrow morning — whichever your CTO prefers. Appreciate the context about the promo batch; we’ll correlate.

Bridge recording and quick diagnostic notes will follow as attachments.

— Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-23T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: initial diagnostics (fastretail latency window)

Quick diagnostic summary from the bridge (10:00 PDT):

Observations:
- Sudden spike aligns with a batch of requests that touched very long contexts (~16k tokens) causing repeated KV-cache misses.
- Autoscaler policy (deployed 2028-06-16) uses a conservative cold-start threshold. When a higher-than-expected fraction of requests required full model loads, nodes were scaling but were not yet warmed — causing elevated p95 and transient errors due to throttling.
- Our rolling batch settings increased effective batch size for the impacted pool during high concurrency, which amplified latency on heavy-context requests.

Preliminary root causes:
1) KV-cache warming disabled for recently-added capacity pools (regression from a config merge).
2) Autoscaler cold-start threshold not tuned for long-context workloads.
3) No short-circuit fallback to a smaller, lower-capacity model variant when context length > 12k tokens.

Immediate remediation applied (10:02 PDT):
- Re-enabled KV-cache pre-warming for the impacted pool. (action: david_kim)
- Lowered batch-window cap for the pool to reduce per-request head-of-line latency. (action: marissa_cole)
- Temporary routing rule to divert 12% of traffic to a warmed sibling pool to reduce load. (action: karthik_iyer)

Next steps for RCA packet and postmortem:
- Collate traces + timeline, export top error stack traces (by 24h).
- Propose an autoscaler policy change and a model-variant fallback (design doc draft in 48h).

I uploaded the raw diagnostic notes to the fastretail RCA folder (link below) and attached a short PDF.

— David

[Attachment: diagnostic-notes-fastretail.pdf]
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@fastretail.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-23T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary & proposed corrective actions — FastRetail latency event (08:45 PDT)

Hi Liam and Sarah,

Thanks again for joining the bridge. Below is our concise executive summary and the corrective action plan we are committing to. We understand the business impact and are prioritizing both short-term mitigation and systemic fixes.

Executive summary:
- Window: 2028-06-23 08:45–09:12 PDT.
- Impact: p95 increased from ~220ms to ~1.1s; error rate peaked at ~6%; affected ~8% of customer requests.
- Root causes (summary): KV-cache pre-warming was disabled for the impacted pool (config regression); autoscaler cold-start threshold not tuned for long-context workloads; batching profile amplified head-of-line latency.

Short-term corrective actions (already started):
1) Re-enable KV-cache pre-warming (completed 10:02 PDT) — reduces cold start overhead.
2) Lower batch-window cap for the pool (completed 10:05 PDT) — lowered head-of-line tail.
3) Temporary traffic diversion to warmed pools (in place) — buys capacity while we fix config.

Planned medium-term actions (60-day roadmap):
A) Autoscaler tuning: implement context-length-aware cold-start thresholds and reduce scale-up ramp time. (owner: Infrastructure team; target: 30 days)
B) Model-variant fallback: automatic fallback to a smaller, low-latency variant for requests with context > 12k tokens. (owner: Model Serve; target: 45 days)
C) Pre-warm verification: add config linting + CI check to prevent disablement of KV pre-warm on pool merges. (owner: Platform QA; target: 14 days)

Operational commitments:
- We will provide a full RCA packet (traces, timeline, error stacks) within 24 hours (delivered to your RCA folder).
- We will run a joint verification test with your ops team next week to validate fixes under a traffic replay. Proposed slots: Tue/Wed next week 09:00–11:00 PDT.
- Executive readout: we can do a concise 20-minute exec call tomorrow 09:00 PDT or Friday 10:00 PDT — please confirm which works for your CTO.

Compensation / SLA: we understand you’ll want SLA remediation details; we will follow the contract process once the incident scope and impact are finalized.

Attachments: bridge-recording-20280623.mp4 (bridge), diagnostic-notes-fastretail.pdf, action-tracker-fastretail.csv (draft).

Let me know preferred time for the exec readout and any additional questions.

— Tessa
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@fastretail.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Patel <sarah@fastretail.com>
Date: 2028-06-23T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident summary & proposed corrective actions — FastRetail latency event (08:45 PDT)

Thanks for the fast triage and the clear plan. We appreciate the traffic diversion and the fixes you already applied.

Couple of asks from our side:
- Please include an estimate of the business impact (failed checkout count, estimated revenue at risk) in the final RCA packet.
- SLA remediation: can you open the credits/exception request pre-emptively while you finalize scope? Our procurement lead (Sarah) will coordinate.
- Exec readout: tomorrow 09:00 PDT works for our CTO. Please send a calendar invite.

Looping Sarah to manage the procurement path.

— Liam
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: david.kim@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam@fastretail.com>, Sarah Patel <sarah@fastretail.com>
Date: 2028-06-24T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Final action tracker and ownership (FastRetail latency event)

Team — consolidated action tracker and owners. Please review and ack by EOD today. I created a short CSV and attached it (action-tracker-fastretail.csv). Key owner items below: 

1) Autoscaler policy changes (design + rollout) — owner: david_kim — target: 2028-07-23 — deliverable: design doc + canary roll plan.
2) Model-variant fallback implementation (prototype) — owner: karthik_iyer — target: 2028-07-08 — deliverable: prototype + perf comparison.
3) CI lint for KV pre-warm config (tests + gating) — owner: marissa_cole — target: 2028-07-07 — deliverable: PR + CI job.
4) Joint verification replay with FastRetail — owner: marissa_cole — target: 2028-06-30 — deliverable: replay results and pass/fail matrix.
5) RCA packet (final, includes revenue impact estimate) — owner: david_kim & Tessa Morgan — target: 2028-06-24 18:00 PDT — deliverable: PDF (uploaded to RCA folder).

Please update the tracker row with notes and status. I will run weekly syncs until the 60-day roadmap items are closed.

Thanks — send any blocking items.

— Tessa
